newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi helicopter transfer pilgrims in no-fly zones.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi helicopter transfer pilgrims in no-fly zones.

text.p: Iraq has started flying its Moslem pilgrims returning from Saudi Arabia to areas within the West's southern and northern no-fly zones, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Friday.
"Helicopters have began transferring pilgrims from the Iraqi-Saudi border to their areas of residence in the provinces," INA said.
INA said the first helicopter was heading towards Mosul 400 km (250 miles) north of Baghdad and well into the northern no-fly zone policed by U.S. and British warplanes based in Turkey.
INA said more helicopters with pilgrims will be heading to other towns within the no-fly zones. U.S., British and French planes guard the air-exclusion zone in southern Iraq.
Earlier this week Iraq sent nine helicopters to the Saudi border in defiance of the U.S. and allied ban on flights in the area.
Washington has said it will not obstruct the helicopter flights but warned Baghdad against building troops in southern Iraq.
